title: Integration tests for marketplace entitlement mapping + org linking (AWS/GCP fixtures) with deterministic retries
creator: Ethan Park
description:
Goal
Add integration test coverage for the end-to-end marketplace provisioning pipeline for both AWS Marketplace and GCP Cloud Marketplace paths:
- Ingest entitlement events (webhook / polling callbacks) -> map external product/SKU identifiers -> create/update internal entitlement(s)
- Drive org linking flow inputs (marketplace account identifier / buyer identifiers) -> ensure correct Redwood org association
- Verify deterministic retry semantics for transient failures and idempotency for duplicate deliveries

Why
We’ve had repeated staging issues where:
- duplicate entitlement events created duplicate entitlements or flipped org links
- retry behavior is non-deterministic (flaky tests) due to real timers/backoff and random ids
- GCP vs AWS payload differences aren’t fully covered, leading to regressions during partner validation

Scope
In scope:
- Integration tests in the control-plane repo using fixture payloads for AWS + GCP entitlement events.
- Deterministic retries: ensure the retry/backoff logic can be exercised with a fake clock or injected scheduler so tests don’t sleep.
- Idempotency assertions: same event delivered N times results in a single entitlement + stable org link.
- Edge cases that are known to break enterprise buyers: region mismatch, wrong org, delayed entitlement activation, and upgrade/downgrade transitions.

Out of scope:
- UI-only Console onboarding wizard tests (covered separately by ENG-4403 and E2E UI automation).
- Performance/load tests.

References
- PRD: sources/confluence/product-docs/requirements/cloud-marketplace-listing-refresh-prd.json
- Onboarding flow spec: sources/confluence/product-docs/design-specs/marketplace-purchase-to-provisioning-onboarding-flow.json
- SKU naming/entitlement IDs ADR: sources/confluence/architecture-and-standards/decision-records/adr-marketplace-sku-naming-and-entitlement-ids.json

Acceptance criteria
1) AWS fixtures
- Given an AWS entitlement notification for a known AWS product code/SKU ID, the mapping layer resolves to the correct internal entitlement(s) and plan codes.
- Duplicate delivery of the same notification is idempotent (no duplicate entitlements; no repeated org-link operations).
- Transient failure in downstream dependency (DB deadlock simulation / external call stub) retries deterministically and succeeds without flake.

2) GCP fixtures
- Given a GCP entitlement event with GCP-specific identifiers, mapping behaves as expected and produces the same internal entitlements as the equivalent AWS SKU in the SKU mapping sheet.
- Handles GCP “entitlement active” vs “pending” states; does not prematurely mark active.

3) Org linking integration
- Given a marketplace buyer identity + link token, the org linking operation attaches the entitlement to the correct Redwood org.
- Prevents cross-org linking if the same marketplace account attempts to link to two orgs without an explicit admin override (expected error code + audit log entry).

4) Deterministic retries
- Tests can force retry attempts without wall-clock waiting.
- Retry attempt count and final outcome are deterministic and asserted.

Test plan (high-level)
- Harness: stand up an ephemeral test DB schema + in-process worker/handler with injected clock + deterministic id generator.
- Fixtures: store canonical AWS + GCP payloads in testdata/marketplace/ (redacted IDs) and maintain a small translation table matching the ADR.
- Assertions:
  - entitlements table rows (count, fields)
  - org_entitlements join correctness
  - audit log events emitted once per logical operation
  - metrics emitted for retry counts (optional if instrumentation is already in place)

Notes / known gotchas
- Ensure tests use fixed timestamps and a fake clock; avoid time.Now() and real sleep.
- If the ingestion path uses async queues, provide a test helper to drain work deterministically.
- Align SKU IDs used in fixtures with latest SKU mapping decisions (PM-873 / ADR) to avoid churn.

Deliverables
- Integration test suite covering AWS + GCP entitlement ingestion and org linking
- Fixture payloads checked into repo with documentation on how to update
- CI stability: <1% flake rate across 20 consecutive runs in main CI pipeline (we’ll spot check pre-merge).
